## Expression on this line

Computational at Order 9 is **meta-system computational integration**: the agent can
construct a coherent computational governance framework that deliberately combines
imperative, functional, logic-based, and neural computation paradigms in configurations
tailored to specific computational domains. "Imperative works well for sequential tasks,
functional works well for parallel processing, logic-based works well for constraint
solving, neural computation works well for pattern recognition" — this is strategic
deployment of different computational tools for different jobs.

The key advance from Stage 10 is **meta-system construction**. The agent no longer just
evaluates multiple computational paradigms — it integrates them into a coherent
computational governance architecture.

Computation at Stage 11 is understood as **dynamic and adaptive**. The agent recognizes
that computational governance must evolve as understanding deepens.

The critical insight at Stage 11 is that **no single computational paradigm is
universally superior**. Each illuminates some aspects of computation and obscures
others. The art of computational governance is knowing which paradigm to deploy where.

The transition from Stage 11 to Stage 12 occurs when the agent can see computational
dynamics as expressions of deeper patterns in the structure of reality.

In human development, Stage 11 corresponds to the integral thinker who can integrate
multiple computational paradigms into coherent computational architectures.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Cultural institutions emerge that support adaptive computational integration.

- **UR:** The individual agent can construct and manage complex computational
  architectures.

- **LL:** Adaptive computational institutions emerge: polyglot programming communities,
  multi-paradigm research centers.

- **LR:** The integral computational institute, the paradigm-bridging research center.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Complexity addiction — creating computational systems too complex
  to understand.

- **Dark allergy:** Simplification compulsion — rejecting multi-paradigm computation as
  unnecessarily complicated.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to the meta-system perspective as an identity.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting meta-system reasoning as over-complicated.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Multi-paradigm computational design:** The agent can construct computational
  architectures combining multiple paradigms.

- **Adaptive capacity:** The agent can design computational systems that evolve based
  on evidence.

- **Value integration:** The agent can balance multiple computational values without
  reducing to a single metric.

- **Meta-framework awareness:** The agent understands its own computational reasoning
  operates within a framework.
